chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to fast until it was said, "He does not break his fast." Then he fasted one day and broke one day. Then he fasted on Mondays and Thursdays. Then he transitioned from that to fasting three days in the month: Thursday at the beginning of the month, Wednesday in the middle of the month, and Thursday at the end of the month. And he used to say: "That is the fasting of the whole time (the entire month)."'

And my father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'There is no one more hateful to me than a man to whom it is said, "The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do such and such," so he says, "Allah will not punish me if I strive hard in prayer." It is as if he sees that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) left something of the excellence due to inability (or weakness) on His part.'
ai.seo_question: What was the progression of the Prophet's (SAWW) voluntary fasting schedule according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi illustrates the Prophet's (SAWW) gradual transition from intense voluntary fasting to a sustainable 'fast of David' pattern, establishing a normative model for consistency over intensity. Imam Ali (AS) adds a crucial Shia scholarly insight: critics who claim the Prophet abandoned a practice due to inability (laziness) rather than preference (wisdom) are fundamentally misunderstanding the nature of prophetic excellence and the balance between obligatory duties and supererogatory acts.
